chunks.arabic_text: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ، الطَّبَرِيُّ، أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، الْخَلِيلِيُّ، (الَّذِي يُقَالُ لَهُ: غُلَامُ خَلِيلٍ، الْآمِلِيُّ). كَذَّابٌ، وَضَّاعٌ لِلْحَدِيثِ، فَاسِدُ [الْمَذْهَبِ] لَا يُلْتَفَتُ إِلَيْهِ.

translations.en: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, al-Ṭabarī, Abū ʿAbdillāh, al-Khalīlī, [of whom it is said: Ghulām Khalil, al-Āmulī]. Liar, fabricator of ḥadīth, corrupt (in madhhab). He is not turned to.

en.summary: This entry from al-Ghada'iri’s *Kitab al-Du'afa* identifies Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad al-Ṭabarī, known as 'Ghulam Khalil,' as a prominent liar (*kadhhab*) whose school of thought is deemed corrupt, rendering his narrations unreliable for Shia jurisprudence. The designation 'Ghulam Khalil' likely refers to his status as a freed slave or servant of a notable figure, a detail often used to distinguish him in biographical dictionaries. His classification as *da'if* (weak) and *kadhhab* (liar) underscores the rigorous scrutiny applied to narrators to preserve the authenticity of the Imams' teachings.
en.seo_question: Who is Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Tabari in Shia hadith sciences?

key_terms.لَا يُلْتَفَتُ إِلَيْهِ: He is not turned to / not relied upon
